title: Everest
subtitle: Base Camp to the summit
sourceNote: South Col route. Camp altitudes vary between seasons and expeditions; summit height is the 2020 Nepal-China survey figure of 8,848.86 m.

waypoints.name: The Khumbu Icefall
waypoints.body: A slow-moving river of ice that shifts a metre a day. Climbers cross it before dawn, on ladders, while it is still frozen solid.

waypoints.name: Camp One
waypoints.body: 6,065 metres, at the top of the icefall. The air here holds about half the oxygen of sea level.

waypoints.name: Camp Two
waypoints.body: 6,400 metres, in the Western Cwm. It is nicknamed the Valley of Silence, and on a still day it is hot enough to burn.

waypoints.name: Camp Three
waypoints.body: 7,162 metres, cut into the Lhotse Face. Tents are pitched on a fifty-degree wall of blue ice.

waypoints.name: The Death Zone
waypoints.body: Above 8,000 metres the body cannot acclimatise. From here on you are dying, and the only cure is to go down.

waypoints.name: Camp Four, the South Col
waypoints.body: 7,906 metres. Most summit attempts leave here around ten at night to reach the top by morning.

waypoints.name: The Balcony
waypoints.body: 8,400 metres. A small platform where climbers change oxygen bottles, usually in the dark.

waypoints.name: The South Summit
waypoints.body: 8,749 metres, and a false top. The real summit is still ahead, along a knife-edge ridge.

waypoints.name: The Hillary Step
waypoints.body: A twelve-metre rock wall at 8,790 metres. It is where queues form, and where queues are dangerous.

waypoints.name: The summit
waypoints.body: 8,848.86 metres. Two thirds of the atmosphere is below you. Nobody stays more than a few minutes.
